title: Article 1: Name & Objectives
paragraphs:
Article 1.1 Name
The name of the organization herein constituted shall be “ChessBlitz YorkU”, abbreviated as “CBYU”

title: Article 2: Definitions
paragraphs:
1. An “executive” refers to a ChessBlitz YorkU executive.
2. An “external event” refers to a chess-related event that is not a ChessBlitz YorkU event.
3. “Collegiate Chess League”, herein abbreviated “CCL” is an international cross-university chess competition created and administered by Chess.com.

title: Article 3: Interpretation
paragraphs:
1. The ChessBlitz YorkU Presidents’ interpretation of the Constitution is the official interpretation of the Constitution.
2. Where the President is not present, the Chair of the meeting will be regarded as the primary source of interpretation of the Constitution and shall be subject to an appeal from meeting members.

title: Article 4: Membership
paragraphs:
1. Membership to ChessBlitz YorkU is open to all York University students, alumni, staff and faculty.
2. There is no membership fee.
3. Every ChessBlitz YorkU member must follow all their York University responsibilities.
4. There exist three (3) levels of membership which are: General Membership, Executive Membership, and Alumni Membership.

Article 4.1: General Membership
Any member who affiliates with the club whether formally (through YUConnect), or informally (through other social media outlets), must be a full-time or part-time student enrolled in a program in the current academic year. Members are entitled to:
* Vote in elections.
* Run for every position in elections except for President and Bookkeeper.
* Participate in general meetings.
* Participate in any activities sponsored by the club.

Article 4.2 Executive Membership
The offered executive positions at ChessBlitz YorkU are:
* President
* Treasurer
* Event Manager
* Outreach Coordinator
* Social Media Coordinator
* Chief Returning Officer
* Tournament Director & Organizer
* CCL Manager
* Community Manager
A member which holds a position on the executive council must be a full-time or part-time student enrolled in a program in the current academic year and is entitled to: 
* Vote in elections.
* Run for any position in elections.
* Participate in all general and executive meetings.
* Participate in and organize all activities sponsored by the club.
* Dedicate a significant amount of time to the club.
* Play a role in making any decision.

Article 4.3 Alumni Membership
An Alumni Member of ChessBlitz YorkU is one who:
* Has previously held a position as a general member or executive member and
* Has graduated from a program at York University.
Alumni Members are entitled to:
* Participate in all general meetings.
* Participate in all executive meetings (provided they have served as an executive in the past and are invited by an executive to join an executive meeting).
* Participate in and organize any activities sponsored by the club.

Article 7: Quorum
paragraphs: The quorum for voting purposes shall be reached when more than 60% of the general members are present, including at least two (2) executives.

title: Article 8: Executive Roles and Duties
paragraphs:
Article 8.1 Executive Composition
The executive members of the club shall be composed of:
* Two (2) Co-Presidents
* One (1) Financial Coordinator
* Four (4) Event Managers
* Three (3) Social Media Coordinators
* Two (2) Outreach Coordinators
* Two (2) Tournament Organizer & Directors
* One (1) CCL Manager
* One (1) Chief Returning Officer
* Two (2) Community Managers

Article 8.2 Duties of General Executive Members
* Attend Executive Meetings
* Represent and support the club positively at all times.
* Each executive member will have a term length of one academic year, starting from the beginning of the Fall semester till the end of the Summer semester of the following year.

Article 8.7 Outreach Coordinator
* This position is limited to two (2) individuals
The Outreach Coordinator must:
* Coordinate communication with YorkU colleges, other York University clubs, chess clubs from other universities, as well as other organizations;
* Strengthen communication between the Canadian University Chess Championship organizers and the ChessBlitz YorkU executive team; and
* Help organize cross-university events such as sub battles.

Article 8.8 Tournament Organizer & Director
* This position is limited to two (2) individuals
The Tournament Organizer & Director must:
* Plan and manage all CFC-rated tournaments and the CUCC qualifier;
* Be familiar with CFC procedures for advertising, administering and reporting rated tournaments;
* Be proficient with SwissSys tournament tracking software; and
* Work with the Presidents to ensure all CFC procedures are followed.

Article 8.10 Chief Returning Officer
* This position is limited to one (1) individual
* The CRO:
   * Shall be appointed one month before election;
   * Shall be a general member of the club or a non-member;
   * Should be an upstanding member of society; and
   * Is familiar with the club, administrative structure, and the mission.
The Chief Returning Officer must:
* Preside, in an independent and transparent manner, over a ChessBlitz YorkU Election and count all votes of a ChessBlitz YorkU Election;
* Not have any conflict of interest in the elections. This includes but is not limited to, running or voting in the ChessBlitz YorkU Elections; and
* Count votes in the election and ensure a smooth transition between executive members.
* Take on the role of the Ombudsperson of the club in charge of any conflict of interest if the current president is absent or unable to deal with the situation.

Article 8.11 Community Manager
* This position is limited to two (2) individuals
The Community Manager must:
* Moderate the CBYU Discord in a fair manner;
* Ensure the rules of the Discord are followed by all members; and
* Report any instances of abuse to the Presidents.

title: Article 9: Elections
paragraphs:
Article 9.2 Application Process
1. The application process applies to the following positions
   a. Chief Returning Officer
   b. Community Manager
   c. All Electoral positions that were not filled during the election with the exception of President and Finance Coordinator
2. When a position becomes available, the organization shall announce the opening to its members and the university community through appropriate channels, such as the organization's website, social media platforms, and email notifications.
3. Interested individuals shall submit applications for open positions within the specified application period. Applications may require submission of a resume, course-schedule or other relevant documents as determined by the organization.
4. The Executive Committee shall act as the Selection Committee responsible for reviewing and evaluation applications.
5. The Selection Committee may conduct interviews with shortlisted candidates to assess their suitability for the position.
6. The Selection Committee shall make decisions regarding the hiring of individuals for open positions via official CBYU channels such as Discord, Email and Instagram. Decisions may be made by consensus or majority vote within the Selection Committee. Successful applicants shall be notified of their selection by email.

title: Article 10: Removal
paragraphs:
1. An executive is removed from the Executive Committee if:
   a. The executive is failing to perform their duties as defined by the ChessBlitz YorkU constitution and by-laws; or
   b. The executive has lost the confidence of other executives.
2. The motion to remove an executive must pass with at least two-thirds of the executive committee voting for the motion.
3. If an executive is removed from the Executive Committee, a by-election for the role of the removed executive is held.

title: Article 11: Amendments
paragraphs:
1. Amendments to the ChessBlitz YorkU constitution and ChessBlitz YorkU bylaws:
   a. are created by executives only;
   b. can be proposed at any time; and
   c. are adopted by a vote of the Executive Committee.
2. A majority of 75% of the executive committee must agree for amendments to be implemented.

title: Article 12: Conflict of Interest
paragraphs:
1. A conflict of interest exists when an executive uses their executive powers in a way that furthers the private interests of themselves or another entity. 
2. If an executive finds themselves in a conflict of interest, they must immediately notify the ChessBlitz YorkU Presidents.
3. If a conflict of interest is found that may affect the executive powers of an executive, either of the ChessBlitz YorkU Presidents may call a meeting wherein the conflict of interest is disclosed to the Executive Committee. In the meeting:
   a. The executive with the alleged conflict of interest may address the Executive Committee about the issue.
   b. A vote by the Executive Committee will then be held on the issue of:
      i. a. whether there is a conflict of interest; and
      ii. b. whether full disclosure is sufficient.
   c. If a vote of no to (3.b.ii) of Article 12 happens, the executive with the conflict of interest must eliminate the conflict of interest.

title: Article 13: Allegations of Wrongdoing
paragraphs:
1. This Article applies when a member alleges that another member has violated this Constitution, the bylaws, applicable York University responsibilities, or another ChessBlitz YorkU rule in a manner that may warrant discipline.
2. Any ChessBlitz YorkU member may submit an allegation in writing to chessblitzyorku@gmail.com or privately to any ChessBlitz YorkU Executive Member. An Executive Member who receives an allegation must promptly forward it to the ChessBlitz YorkU Presidents, unless a President is named in the allegation or has a conflict of interest.
3. The ChessBlitz YorkU Presidents will oversee the investigation. A person who is named in the allegation, directly involved in the events, or otherwise has a conflict of interest must not investigate, review, or vote on the matter. If a President must recuse themselves, the Chief Returning Officer will assume that President's responsibilities under this Article. If the Chief Returning Officer must also recuse themselves or is unavailable, the eligible members of the Executive Committee will appoint an impartial Executive Member or club member to conduct the investigation.
4. The person responsible for the investigation must acknowledge the allegation in writing within 48 hours of receiving it. The respondent must be notified of the substance of the allegation with enough detail to provide a response, subject to reasonable safety and privacy considerations.
5. The investigation must begin promptly and, where reasonably possible, be completed within 14 days after the allegation is received. The investigator will:
   a. review the written allegation and relevant club records;
   b. give the complainant and respondent separate opportunities to provide a statement, documents, and other relevant information;
   c. speak with relevant witnesses when necessary; and
   d. keep a written record of the information reviewed and the findings.
6. The investigator's findings must be presented to the eligible members of the Executive Committee. Eligibility is limited to members who are not named in the allegation, were not directly involved in the events, and do not otherwise have a conflict of interest.
7. Before any decision is made, the respondent must receive a summary of the findings and a reasonable opportunity to provide a defence or response.
8. Quorum for a decision under this Article is more than one-half of the eligible members of the Executive Committee. A finding of wrongdoing and any resulting discipline require a majority of the votes cast. Removal of an Executive Member must also satisfy the two-thirds voting requirement in Article 10.
9. If wrongdoing is confirmed, the eligible members of the Executive Committee will determine proportionate discipline, which may include censure, suspension, removal or impeachment, or another corrective measure permitted by this Constitution.
10. A written decision, including the reasons and any resulting action, must be provided to the complainant and respondent no later than 21 days after the allegation was received. A non-confidential version of the decision must be made available upon request to members of ChessBlitz YorkU or York University.
11. No person may retaliate against a complainant, respondent, witness, investigator, or decision-maker for participating in good faith in a process under this Article. Information must be shared only as reasonably necessary to investigate and decide the matter.

title: Article 14: Complaints Process
paragraphs:
1. This Article applies to complaints about a ChessBlitz YorkU decision, service, event, procedure, accessibility issue, administration, or the organization as a whole. A complaint that alleges wrongdoing by a member or may result in discipline must be handled under Article 13. If a submission raises both types of issues, the written acknowledgement must identify which issues will be handled under each Article.
2. ChessBlitz YorkU will administer this complaints process in a manner consistent with the principles of openness, accessibility, and democracy in the Regulation Regarding Student Organizations Schedule D.
3. Any ChessBlitz YorkU member may submit a complaint in writing to chessblitzyorku@gmail.com or privately to any ChessBlitz YorkU Executive Member. An Executive Member who receives a complaint must promptly forward it to the ChessBlitz YorkU Presidents. An accessible alternative to a written submission will be provided upon request.
4. The complainant must receive a written acknowledgement within 48 hours after the complaint is received. The acknowledgement must identify the person responsible for the review, the process that will be followed, and the expected decision date.
5. The ChessBlitz YorkU Presidents will coordinate the review. A person who is named in the complaint, directly involved in the matter, or otherwise has a conflict of interest must not review or vote on the complaint. If a President must recuse themselves, the Chief Returning Officer will assume that President's responsibilities under this Article. If the Chief Returning Officer must also recuse themselves or is unavailable, the eligible members of the Executive Committee will appoint an impartial Executive Member or club member to conduct the review.
6. The person responsible for the review will: 
   a. confirm the issues raised and the outcome requested by the complainant;
   b. review relevant records, policies, and prior decisions;
   c. give the complainant and any person affected by the complaint separate opportunities to provide relevant information; and 
   d. prepare written findings and recommended actions.
7. The findings will be presented to the eligible members of the Executive Committee, excluding anyone named in the complaint, directly involved in the matter, or otherwise in a conflict of interest. Quorum is more than one-half of the eligible members, and a decision requires a majority of the votes cast.
8. The eligible members of the Executive Committee may correct or reconsider a decision, provide an accessibility measure, change a policy or procedure, require training, refer an allegation to Article 13, or take another action permitted by this Constitution.
9. A written decision, including the reasons and any resulting action, must be provided to the complainant no later than 21 days after the complaint was received. A non-confidential version of the decision must be made available upon request to members of ChessBlitz YorkU.
10. No person may retaliate against a complainant, participant, reviewer, or decision-maker for participating in good faith in a process under this Article. Information must be shared only as reasonably necessary to review and decide the complaint.

title: Article 15: Financial Responsibility
paragraphs:
1. The ChessBlitz YorkU Presidents are the only signing authorities of ChessBlitz YorkU.
2. The ChessBlitz YorkU Finances Coordinator is responsible for managing the ChessBlitz YorkU budget as well as managing and approving all ChessBlitz YorkU financial records in consultation with the ChessBlitz YorkU Presidents.
3. If ChessBlitz YorkU folds, any remaining funds of ChessBlitz YorkU must be donated to charity.
